title: PowerPoint to Video – Turn PPTX Slides into MP4 Free
description: Turn a PowerPoint deck into an MP4 or WebM video in your browser: each slide shown for the seconds you choose, in 1080p or 720p. Nothing is uploaded.
heading: Convert PowerPoint to Video
subtitle: Turn your PowerPoint slides into an MP4 or WebM video, each slide on screen for the seconds you choose; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert PPTX to MP4 without PowerPoint: each slide is drawn the way this site's PowerPoint viewer (beta) shows it, then held on screen for 1 to 30 seconds in a 1080p or 720p video. A 12-slide deck at 5 seconds a slide gives a one-minute video. Slides don't move, so a low frame rate keeps the file small and the video is made quickly. Handy for a looping screen in a lobby, a slide show for social media, or a deck someone can watch on a phone. Works with .pptx, .ppsx, .potx and .pptm files, and the video is made with the encoders built into your browser.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your deck is drawn and turned into a video by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Your timing
features.text: Choose how long each slide stays on screen, from 1 to 30 seconds, and which slides to include.

features.title: MP4 or WebM
features.text: Full HD 1080p or 720p, in the slide's own shape, ready to play almost anywhere.

stepsTitle: How to turn PowerPoint into a video

steps.title: Choose your presentation
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a .pptx, .ppsx, .potx or .pptm file on the page.

steps.title: Set the timing
steps.text: Pick the seconds per slide, the size and the format; type slide numbers if you want only some of them.

steps.title: Make the video
steps.text: Click Make video. The slides are drawn one by one, then the video is put together.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Play the video on the page and download it.

handles: Text, shapes, tables and pictures saved in the file.
Widescreen 16:9 and standard 4:3 slides, the video in the slide's shape.
Output: MP4 or WebM, 1920 or 1280 pixels wide, with no sound.
limits: Animations, slide transitions, embedded videos and audio are not included: each slide is a still picture.
The slides follow this site's PowerPoint viewer, which is in beta; fonts aren't embedded, so web fonts and fonts your browser doesn't have may look different.
There is no voice-over or music; the video is silent.
Every slide is kept in memory while the video is made, so very long decks may need 720p or fewer slides.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The slides are drawn and the video is made by your own browser, on your device; neither the deck nor the video is sent anywhere.

faq.question: How long will the video be?
faq.answer: The number of slides times the seconds per slide: 10 slides at 5 seconds make a 50-second video.

faq.question: Are animations and transitions kept?
faq.answer: No. Each slide is shown as a still picture, as it looks once all its animations have finished, and slides change with a cut. Embedded videos and audio are left out too.

faq.question: Can I add a voice-over or music?
faq.answer: Not here: the video is silent. Add a sound track afterwards with Add audio to video.

faq.question: Why is the frame rate so low?
faq.answer: Slides don't move, so a low frame rate keeps the file small and makes the video quickly; it looks the same as a higher one.

faq.question: Which browsers can make the video?
faq.answer: Recent Chrome and Edge make both MP4 and WebM; other browsers may make only one. If yours can't make the chosen format, the page says so and you can pick the other.

faq.question: Can I get pictures or a PDF instead?
faq.answer: Yes. PowerPoint to JPG saves each slide as a picture, and PowerPoint to PDF saves one page per slide.
